blue.$comment: Steps 200–400 exist for the dark theme, not the light one: there the `primary` ramp has to go UP on hover/active, because the background lightens under the dark `on-primary` text. Going down (as in light) drove the button label's contrast to 3.45:1 and 2.66:1 — measured when the policy started counting those pairs at all.

slate.$comment-1000: The ramp's endpoint, and it exists for exactly one reader: `pct.scrim` in the DARK theme. A veil has to darken a page that is already `slate.900`, and 900 over 900 dims by nothing — so the step below it is the only value that works there. The light theme's veil is `slate.900`, which is why this is a step of the ramp and not a literal in the component tier (req-token-tiers).

green.$comment: The palette's first green. It began as two steps for a tone that only painted an icon; the family below is what a toned control needs instead — `700`/`800`/`900` for the fill, its hover and its press on the light theme, `400`/`300`/`200` for the same three on the dark, and `100`/`200` as the soft face's tint with the label on it. Every step is the same scale the other hues come from, so a tone is a colour the skin already knew how to make rather than a hue somebody picked. `700` is still where it clears 4.5:1 as text on the light surface (5.02:1) and `400` where it clears it on the dark (10.25:1).

amber.$comment: The same family for the warning tone, and the levels are measurements rather than a mirror of green's: an amber light enough to read as a warning is dark enough to fail as text, so `700` is where it clears 4.5:1 on white (5.02:1) and `400` where it clears it on `slate.900` (10.69:1). A `600` amber, which is the shade most palettes reach for, measures 3.19:1 on white — enough for a UI edge and not for a word.

red.$comment: The error ramp, and the only one here that LOST a step: `600` left with the tone axis, because `danger` moved to `700` the day a quiet button face had to carry the label on the page's own hover tint — `red.600` reads 4.41:1 there, and the policy gate blocks a build on it. That also put danger on the rule green and amber were already keeping: a tone's base is the first step that carries white text. What the rest of the ramp is for is the family a toned CONTROL needs beyond a single colour — a resting fill, a hover, a press, a tint and the word standing on it, twice over because the dark theme answers with the other end of the same scale.

target.$comment: Minimum touch area per WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (24x24 px).

control.$comment: Control height at a given size — the axis shared by the button and the field row. The height is a value outright here, not the outcome of padding and line height: only then are a field and a button of the same size equal by definition (req-api-size).

motion.$comment: Motion is a token axis, not an exception in a component stylesheet: only that makes `prefers-reduced-motion` apply across the whole library from one rule (req-a11y-motion). The split is not by speed but by KIND of motion, because reduction does two different things to them: a state transition is to disappear, a continuous indicator (a spinner) only to slow down — stopped, it would no longer report that the button is working.

violet.$comment: Two steps, and the second is not a spare: `600` is the gradient's middle stop on a light ground, `400` the same stop on a dark one — the brand's own violet measures 3.13:1 as TEXT against the dark surface, which is legal for an edge at 3:1 and not for a word at 4.5:1 (0065).

cyan.$comment: The same pair, and the LEVEL is a measurement rather than a mirror of violet's: `cyan.400` reads 9.88:1 on the dark surface against violet.400's 6.56 and blue.400's 7.02, so the sweep would have one end that shouts. `500` lands at 7.35 and the three stand together.
